architecture.mechanism: Transmission output drag measured as a function of speed while in neutral can be modeled as a second-order expression (F0 + F1*V + F2*V^2), and the deviation between the quadratic regression and the measured drag at individual velocities can be significant — providing a quantitative signature that isolates individual transmission loss sources.
architecture.intervention: Run a modified neutral "coastdown test" on the 2019 Silverado 1500 eight-speed transmission to measure output drag versus speed, fit the quadratic F0 + F1*V + F2*V^2, and compare the regression to measured drag at the 40–60 mph shudder band; use the localized deviation to isolate the torque converter clutch as the individual loss source, then replace the torque converter clutch (and fluid) to eliminate that loss component.
architecture.expected_effect: The speed-resolved drag deviation isolates the torque converter clutch loss, enabling targeted elimination of the clutch shudder, vibration, and shift hesitation under acceleration.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure output drag vs. speed in neutral before and after torque converter clutch replacement; if the deviation between the quadratic regression and measured drag at 40–60 mph does not decrease after replacement, the mechanism is falsified and the loss source lies elsewhere.
